(Courtesy Matthew Murphy/BroadwaySF) The stage musical “Some Like It Hot,” now at the Orpheum Theatre in San Francisco, is a delightful mix of the old and new—a simply swell adaptation of the 1959 classic film comedy about two cross-dressing musicians trying to escape a mobster after they witness a hit.

And yet, if it’s possible to redeem this film, the charmingly vibrant “Some Like It Hot” musical, playing on tour as part of the RBTL season at West Herr Auditorium Theater through May 18, comes pretty darn close.
But the overall effect is of a musical uneasily straddling revamp and novelty.

cn.t: Critics praise this touring production as a dazzling, high-energy spectacle with top-notch choreography and performances. Most laud its modern update addressing gender identity, though a few question whether the cross-dressing premise feels outdated.
